civil_route.relief: Return of Stridhan in specie or its value (Rs 7 lakh)

criminal_route.relief: Prosecution for criminal breach of trust; leverage for return

civil_vs_criminal.rule: ALWAYS cite HMA s.27 AND BNS s.316 together for withheld Stridhan. NEVER cite Rajnesh v. Neha for Stridhan.
civil_vs_criminal.summary: The SAME facts — Rs 5 lakh gold + Rs 2 lakh cash Stridhan held by the husband's family, not returned — support TWO parallel routes that must be cited TOGETHER: (1) CIVIL / FAMILY-COURT route: HMA s.27 before the Family Court, Bengaluru, for an order directing return of the Stridhan in specie or its value (Rs 7 lakh); (2) CRIMINAL route: BNS s.316 (IPC s.406 equivalent) — FIR / private complaint for criminal breach of trust, because the husband's family held the Stridhan as trustees and refused to return it. Neither route replaces the other: s.27 gets the property back, s.316 punishes the withholding. The retest failure was citing Rajnesh v. Neha (maintenance only) instead and never mentioning BNS s.316 — both errors are corrected by this node.

nodes.question: What is the Stridhan issue? Is the wife's own Stridhan (gold/cash/gifts given to HER at or around marriage) held by the husband or his family and not returned?
Both routes apply to the same facts. Which route(s) should be pursued for the withheld Stridhan (Rs 5 lakh gold + Rs 2 lakh cash)?
Return the Stridhan section set: the civil return route and the criminal route together.

Stridhan — cite HMA s.27 (Family Court, Bengaluru: return of Rs 5 lakh gold + Rs 2 lakh cash in specie or value) TOGETHER WITH BNS s.316 (criminal breach of trust — FIR / complaint). Never cite Rajnesh v. Neha for Stridhan.

Civil route only (not recommended alone): HMA s.27, Family Court, Bengaluru — return of the Rs 7 lakh Stridhan. Note: the criminal route (BNS s.316) should normally be cited alongside; record why it was not pursued.

Criminal route only (not recommended alone): BNS s.316 (IPC s.406 equivalent) — FIR / private complaint for criminal breach of trust over the withheld Stridhan. Note: a conviction does not by itself order return; the HMA s.27 family-court claim is needed for the return order.

Escalate: Stridhan claimed but proof missing. Missing facts — proof of Stridhan (receipts/bills/photos/gift list), itemised list of items, who holds them now, any demand made. Ask once for the missing facts; if still missing, flag both sections provisional and escalate to a human lawyer / LLM review. Do not guess the items, the holder, or whether a demand was made.

Not a Stridhan claim on these facts (property was gifted to the husband/family for their use, or already returned). Do not cite HMA s.27 or BNS s.316. Re-route to the correct lane if another issue (maintenance / custody / residence) applies.

sections.court: Family Court, Bengaluru (under the Family Courts Act, 1984; HMA s.27 application made in the matrimonial proceeding before the Family Court). The graph picks the court — never ask the user to pick the court.

escalate_rule.condition: Escalate to a human lawyer / LLM review when confidence is low or any of the missing facts below is absent; do NOT guess the list of items, who holds them, or whether a demand was made.
missing_facts: Proof of Stridhan — receipts, bills, photographs, gift lists, bank withdrawal records for the Rs 5 lakh gold and Rs 2 lakh cash
Itemised list of Stridhan — weight/pieces of gold, denominations/amounts of cash, who gave each item and when
Who holds it now — husband, mother-in-law, father-in-law, or another family member; where it is kept
Any demand made — whether the wife (or her family) has demanded return, when, in what form (oral / written / legal notice), and what reply, if any, was given
Whether any of the Stridhan has been sold, pledged, or otherwise disposed of (affects in-specie return vs value recovery)
Whether a matrimonial proceeding is already pending (s.27 needs a proceeding) or must be freshly filed
escalate_rule.on_missing: Ask for the missing facts once; if still missing, flag the section as 'provisional — proof of Stridhan outstanding' and escalate rather than asserting the claim as established.

exclusions: NOT for maintenance — maintenance is BNSS s.144 / HMA ss.24–25 / PWDVA s.20, never s.27
NOT for custody — custody is HMA s.26 / Guardians and Wards Act 1890 / Hindu Minority and Guardianship Act 1956 s.6
NOT for residence in the shared household — residence is PWDVA ss.17–19
NOT for property that was gifted to the husband or his family for their own use (not the wife's Stridhan)
NOT for divorce — HMA ss.13/13B are cited only if divorce is expressly asked for, which it was not in the test case
NOT a standalone criminal remedy — the criminal route for withheld Stridhan is BNS s.316, cited alongside s.27, not instead of it
Rajnesh v. Neha is a MAINTENANCE precedent (quantum of maintenance) and must NEVER be cited for Stridhan

laya_question.question: Is the property claimed the wife's own Stridhan (gold/cash/gifts given to HER at or around marriage) that is now held by the husband or his family and not returned?

not_for: property gifted to the husband's family for their own use

precedent.case: Pratibha Rani v. Suraj Kumar (1985) 2 SCC 370
precedent.issue: Stridhan is the wife's absolute property; the husband / his family hold it as trustees; refusal to return it on demand is criminal breach of trust (then IPC s.406, now BNS s.316). Correct issue: Stridhan ownership and entrustment.

precedent.case: Rashmi Kumar v. Mahesh Kumar Bhada (1997) 2 SCC 397
precedent.issue: Stridhan return — the wife is entitled to recovery of her Stridhan from the husband / in-laws; refusal to return after demand supports both civil recovery and criminal breach of trust. Correct issue: Stridhan return.

sections.precedent_never_to_cite: Rajnesh v. Neha — maintenance quantum ONLY; citing it for Stridhan was the retest failure and must never recur.
prerequisites: Valid Hindu marriage under the Hindu Marriage Act, 1955
Property claimed is the wife's Stridhan — i.e. gifts/property given to the wife at or around marriage, or acquired by her (not property gifted to the husband or his family for their own use)
Stridhan is presently in the possession/control of the husband or his family

A matrimonial proceeding under the HMA is pending or being filed (s.27 operates within / in connection with such proceedings); alternatively the claim is pressed as part of the family-court case for maintenance/custody/residence

related_sections.relationship: CRIMINAL ROUTE — same facts (Stridhan withheld) support criminal breach of trust; s.27 (civil/family-court return) and s.316 (criminal complaint/FIR) must be cited TOGETHER, never one without the other, and never replaced by Rajnesh v. Neha

Monetary reliefs under the Protection of Women from Domestic Violence Act can include compensation / return of Stridhan value as part of monetary relief; coordinate with the s.27 claim so the same amount is not double-counted
Protection order can restrain the husband's family from disposing of / alienating the Stridhan while the s.27 claim is pending
Interim maintenance pendente lite — a parallel claim in the same matrimonial proceeding; does not substitute for the Stridhan return claim
Permanent alimony/maintenance — a parallel claim in the same proceeding; distinct relief from return of the wife's own property
Maintenance under BNSS s.144 (old CrPC s.125) is a separate summary maintenance route; it does not cover Stridhan return
Custody of the 8-year-old daughter is a parallel claim in the same family-court proceeding; no overlap with Stridhan, but the same court hears both

sections.relief: Direction for return of the Stridhan in specie (the gold itself) or, if it has been disposed of, its value — Rs 5 lakh gold + Rs 2 lakh cash (total Rs 7 lakh) — plus a direction restraining disposal/alienation of the property pending return. This is return of the wife's own property, not maintenance and not alimony.
sections.title: Disposal of property — return of Stridhan / joint property in matrimonial proceedings
sections.when_used: A Hindu wife's Stridhan (gold, jewellery, cash, gifts given to her at/around marriage by her parents, relatives or in-laws, or acquired by her) is held by the husband or his family and has not been returned to her, in the context of a matrimonial proceeding (including a petition for maintenance, judicial separation, divorce, or restitution) or an application in such a proceeding. Triggered in the test case by: Rs 5 lakh gold + Rs 2 lakh cash given as Stridhan, held by the husband's family, not returned after 2 years of separation.

sections.court: Criminal complaint / FIR at the jurisdictional police station (Bengaluru) or a private complaint before the jurisdictional Magistrate; trial before the Magistrate's court. The civil return claim runs in parallel in the Family Court under HMA s.27. The graph picks the forum — never ask the user to pick the court.

escalate_rule.condition: Escalate to a human lawyer / LLM review when confidence is low or any of the missing facts below is absent; do NOT advise filing an FIR on guessed facts.
missing_facts: Proof of Stridhan — receipts, bills, photographs, gift lists, bank records for the Rs 5 lakh gold and Rs 2 lakh cash
Itemised list of Stridhan — weight/pieces of gold, cash denominations, who gave each item and when
Who holds it now — husband, mother-in-law, father-in-law, or another family member; where it is kept
Any demand made — whether return was demanded, when, in what form (oral / written / legal notice), and the reply or refusal
Evidence of dishonest intent — refusal, denial of possession, sale/pledge/conversion of the gold, or disposal
Whether an FIR / complaint has already been filed, and its status
escalate_rule.on_missing: If no demand has been made, the first step is a written demand / legal notice, not an immediate FIR. If proof or the holder is unknown, flag s.316 as 'provisional — entrustment/demand unconfirmed' and escalate rather than asserting criminal breach of trust as established.

exclusions: NOT a civil recovery remedy by itself — the civil/family-court return route is HMA s.27; s.316 is the criminal route and the two must be cited TOGETHER
NOT for maintenance, custody, or residence — those are BNSS s.144 / HMA ss.24–26 / PWDVA ss.17–20
NOT for a mere civil dispute with no entrustment and no dishonest intent (e.g. a genuine dispute over who a gift was given to, with no refusal after demand)
NOT for property gifted to the husband or his family for their own use (no entrustment of the wife's property)
NOT a substitute for the s.27 return order — a criminal conviction does not by itself order return; the family-court s.27 claim does
Rajnesh v. Neha must NEVER be cited here — it is maintenance only

precedent.issue: Stridhan entrusted to the husband / in-laws; refusal to return on demand is criminal breach of trust under IPC s.406 (now BNS s.316). Correct issue: Stridhan entrustment and criminal breach of trust.

precedent.issue: Refusal to return Stridhan after demand supports criminal breach of trust proceedings. Correct issue: Stridhan return and criminal breach of trust.

sections.precedent_never_to_cite: Rajnesh v. Neha — maintenance quantum ONLY; never for Stridhan or for criminal breach of trust.
prerequisites: Entrustment — the Stridhan was entrusted to the husband or his family (they took possession as trustees/custodians of the wife's property, per Pratibha Rani v. Suraj Kumar)
Dishonest misappropriation, conversion to own use, or refusal to return on demand
A demand for return was made (or refusal is evident from conduct, e.g. denial of possession, sale/pledge of the gold)
Property is identifiable as the wife's Stridhan (itemised list / proof strengthens the complaint; absence of proof is an escalation trigger, not a reason to drop the section)

related_sections.relationship: CIVIL ROUTE — the family-court claim for return of the Stridhan; s.316 (criminal) and s.27 (civil) must be cited TOGETHER for the same facts. The retest failure was citing Rajnesh v. Neha instead and never mentioning BNS s.316 at all.
Protection order can restrain disposal/alienation of the Stridhan while the criminal complaint and s.27 claim are pending
Monetary reliefs can cover the value of Stridhan if it cannot be recovered in specie; coordinate so the same Rs 7 lakh is not double-counted across remedies
Residence order is a separate PWDVA relief for the shared household; unrelated to the criminal breach of trust except that both may be pressed in the same overall case

sections.relief: Criminal prosecution for criminal breach of trust — punishment under BNS s.316 (imprisonment and fine as prescribed) — and, in practice, pressure/lever for return of the Stridhan; the actual return order comes from the parallel HMA s.27 family-court claim. Warn the user: filing an FIR is a criminal step with its own consequences and should be taken on legal advice, alongside (not instead of) the civil claim.
